tells.1: Slightly flattened, trimmed phrasing ('nights that end', 'cooks want to work for you') that loses some of the voice's rhythm and specificity
tells.2: Bold label-colon section headers ('What you'll do:', 'What we're after:') are a common template pattern, though normal for job posts
tells.3: Forced casual insertions ('honestly, that's the fun part', 'your opinion will actually count') and a run of sentences starting with 'You'll'

reason: Version 2 keeps the strongest, most natural kitchen voice ('slammed on the weekends', 'the kind of person cooks want to work for'), and its headers help candidates scan the post. Version 3 reads like a humanizer pass that adds conversational filler and weakens the confident tone.
